exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Steal or Forge Authentication Certificates
exploitedBy.relevance: Absence of mutual TLS allows an attacker to bypass certificate-based authentication, enabling theft or forgery of credentials used during artifact push.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: SIP and Trust Provider Hijacking
exploitedBy.relevance: Without mutual TLS, trust validation during artifact push can be subverted, similar to hijacking trust providers to accept unauthorized artifacts.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Symmetric Cryptography
exploitedBy.relevance: Weak or expired TLS cipher negotiation undermines the symmetric encryption layer protecting data in transit, enabling interception or decryption of communications.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Asymmetric Cryptography
exploitedBy.relevance: Expired or weak TLS ciphers compromise asymmetric key exchange mechanisms, allowing adversaries to perform downgrade or man-in-the-middle attacks.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Credentials in Registry
exploitedBy.relevance: Overprivileged write tokens for pipeline service identities are a form of excessive credential exposure that attackers can harvest and abuse.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Application Access Token
exploitedBy.relevance: Bearer token replay directly maps to the use of stolen application access tokens to authenticate and push artifacts to a registry without valid credentials.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Steal Application Access Token
exploitedBy.relevance: The attack vector involves stealing a bearer token to replay it for unauthorized registry push operations.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Code Signing Certificates
exploitedBy.relevance: Removing SBOM and signatures from artifacts in transit directly targets the code signing verification chain used to authenticate artifact provenance.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Indicator Removal
exploitedBy.relevance: Stripping SBOMs and signatures is a form of indicator removal, eliminating evidence of tampering and provenance metadata from artifacts.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Exfiltration Over Alternative Protocol
exploitedBy.relevance: Fallback to plaintext protocols creates an unencrypted channel that adversaries can exploit for data exfiltration over alternative, unprotected protocols.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Protocol Tunneling
exploitedBy.relevance: Plaintext protocol fallback can be abused by attackers to tunnel malicious traffic through unencrypted channels, bypassing security controls.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Invalid Code Signature
exploitedBy.relevance: Without content-addressable integrity verification, artifacts with invalid or absent signatures can be pushed undetected, directly relating to this technique.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Poisoned Pipeline Execution
exploitedBy.relevance: Without content-addressable integrity checks, malicious artifacts can be injected into the pipeline, enabling poisoned pipeline execution.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Automated Collection
exploitedBy.relevance: Absent rate limiting on the write path allows automated, high-volume operations such as bulk artifact uploads or automated abuse of the write API.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: DNS Server
exploitedBy.relevance: DNS spoofing to redirect artifact push traffic directly involves compromising or manipulating DNS infrastructure to point to a rogue registry.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: DNS
exploitedBy.relevance: The attack leverages DNS protocol manipulation to redirect artifact push operations to an attacker-controlled registry.
